title: Graydon Exception to Public Bidding and Nutrition Services Food Contract - Sysco San Francisco, Inc. - Chief Systems and Services Officer
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0001 - Authorizing Use of Graydon Exception to Public Bidding for Nutrition Services Food Contract With Sysco San Francisco, Inc and Approving Nutrition Services Food Contract With Sysco San Francisco, Inc, Fremont, CA, for the latter to provide supplemental food products and supplies to supplement items, including meat, poultry, high protein foods and fresh produce for the District’s student meal program, for the term August 12, 2021 through December 31, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $2,000,000.00.
headline: Buys up to $2M in food from Sysco for student meals through Dec. 2021 without a public bid
summary: The district is hiring Sysco San Francisco to supply extra meat, poultry, high-protein foods and fresh produce for its student meal program from August 12 to December 31, 2021. The district is skipping its own public bidding by using a legal exception to public bidding (called the Graydon exception). The contract is capped at $2,000,000.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
title: Agreement for Materials Testing Services – Consolidated Engineering Laboratories – Lincoln Elementary School Water Intrusion Repairs Project
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Agreement for Materials Testing Services by and between the District and Consolidated Engineering Laboratories, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide materials testing and construction inspection services for the Lincoln Elementary School Water Intrusion Repairs Project, in the amount of $26,367.00 for basic services, with the District adding a 10% contingency fee of $10,000 for additional services, if needed, for a total not to exceed amount of $36,367.00, with work scheduled to commence on June 16, 2021, and scheduled to last until August 23, 2021, but may not be completed until later if delays in design or construction arise.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Pays Consolidated Engineering Laboratories up to $36,367 for testing at Lincoln Elementary repairs
summary: Consolidated Engineering Laboratories will provide materials testing and construction inspection for the water intrusion repairs at Lincoln Elementary School. The price is $26,367 for basic services plus $10,000 held for additional services if needed, for a cap of $36,367. Work was scheduled to start June 16, 2021, before this vote, and to run through August 23, 2021, though it may last longer if delays arise.
source_issue: The text calls the $10,000 contingency a 10% fee, but 10% of the $26,367.00 base amount would be about $2,637; the contract sets the contingency at a flat $10,000, and the stated $36,367.00 total is correct.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement - District and Brandman University - Intern Partnership and Practica Programs - K-12 Teaching - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Memorandum of Understanding Interagency Agreement (MOUIA) by and between the District and Brandman University (University or BU), a California nonprofit, private university, applying to K-12 Teaching, including Education Specialist, School Counselor, Clinical School Psychologist, and Administrative Services, and other Pupil Personnel Services credentials and certifications, as may be specified, for the term July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024, pursuant to the terms and conditions of the MOUIA.
headline: Renews Brandman University partnership for teacher, counselor and psychologist interns through 2024
summary: The district and Brandman University, a private nonprofit university, renew an agreement for intern and practicum placements. It covers K-12 teaching, education specialist, school counselor, clinical school psychologist and administrative services credentials, plus other student support credentials. It runs from July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2024. The text does not state a dollar amount.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Data Sharing Agreement - The Oakland Public Education Fund, The Oakland REACH, CARES for Learning, and The New Teacher Project (TNTP) - Research, Assessment, and Data (RAD) Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Data Sharing Agreement 2020-2021 by and between District and The Oakland Public Education Fund, The Oakland REACH, CARES for Learning, and The New Teacher Project (TNTP), authorizing District to share data with the latter recipients, in order for recipients to use student-level data in order to understand students prior reading performance, monitor and support individual students literacy growth and overall school engagement, accurately communicate with families about student progress, and support families as needed in all aspects of their child’s school experience, as set forth in Exhibit A, for the period of April 21, 2021 through June 30, 2022, at no cost to the District.
headline: Shares student data at no cost with Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland REACH and two others
summary: The district will share student-level data with The Oakland Public Education Fund, The Oakland REACH, CARES for Learning, and The New Teacher Project (TNTP). The groups will use it to understand students' earlier reading performance, track literacy growth and school engagement, keep families informed, and support families. The agreement covers April 21, 2021 to June 30, 2022 and costs the district nothing.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No.1, Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Be The Change Consulting - Chief of Staff
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Agreement between the District and Be The Change Consulting, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide facilitation of process design team meetings [for the George Floyd Safety Plan], as specified in “Section 2 - Services” of Agreement, incorporated herein as though fully set forth, in the additional amount of $18,500.00, increasing the not to exceed amount of the Agreement from $30,000.00 to $48,500.00, for the period of April 1, 2021, through June 30, 2021.  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $18,500 for Be The Change Consulting to run George Floyd Safety Plan design meetings
summary: The board ratifies, meaning approves after the fact, a change that raises the contract with Be The Change Consulting from $30,000 to $48,500, an added $18,500. The firm facilitates process design team meetings for the George Floyd Safety Plan. The amendment covers April 1 to June 30, 2021, which was already over before this vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: General Services Agreement – School Facility Consultants – Facilities Planning & Management Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of General Services Agreement by and between the District and School Facility Consultants (SFC), Sacramento, CA, for the latter to provide the following services, among others, to assist the District on an ongoing basis to determine and acquire State funding eligibility for new school construction, the modernization of existing school facilities and joint-use projects under the School Facility Program;  assist the District with the preparation and submittal of California Department of Education and   State   Allocation   Board   applications  required   for   eligible   new construction   and modernization projects; assist the District with accessing new funding programs as applicable;  assist  the  District  with  accessing  additional  eligibility  that  may  be  generated  through  AB 1014; and to perform other services specified in the SFC proposal of May 14, 2021, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the Facilities Planning & Management Project, in the not-to-exceed amount of $190,000.00, for the term July 1, 2021, through June 30, 2022.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Pays School Facility Consultants up to $190,000 to help win state school construction funding
summary: School Facility Consultants will help the district work out and claim state funding eligibility for new school construction, modernization and joint-use projects. That includes preparing applications to the California Department of Education and the State Allocation Board. The contract is capped at $190,000 for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor - Competitively Bid – Data Media Services, Inc. – Various Video Surveillance Project – Division of Facilities Planning & Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Agreement By and Between District [Owner] and Data Media Services, Inc., Stockton, CA [Contractor] [Competitively Bid], for the latter to provide installation of 25 exterior cameras, programming of the servers and software for the Video Surveillance Project at various District sites, including Oakland Technical High School, Melrose Leadership Academy TK-2 (5328 Brann - Sherman Campus), and Melrose Leadership Academy 3-8 (4730 Fleming - Maxwell Park Campus), in the amount of $62,000.00, which includes a contingency of $6,000.00, as the lowest responsive bidder, and authorizing the President and Secretary of the Board to sign the Agreement for same with said bidder, with the work anticipated to commence on August 12, 2021, and scheduled to last for ninety (90) days, with an anticipated ending date of November 10, 2021.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Awards Data Media Services $62,000 to install 25 security cameras at Oakland Tech and Melrose sites
summary: Data Media Services, the lowest responsive bidder in a competitive bid, will install 25 exterior cameras and program the servers and software for the Video Surveillance Project. Sites include Oakland Technical High School and two Melrose Leadership Academy campuses. The $62,000 includes a $6,000 contingency. Work is expected to run 90 days, from August 12 to November 10, 2021.
schools: Oakland Technical High School; Melrose Leadership Academy TK-2; Melrose Leadership Academy 3-8
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: General Services Agreement – Xebec Data Corporation – Prop 39 Energy Operations Facilities Planning & Management Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of General Services Agreement by and between the District and Xebec Data Corporation, Lafayette, Colorado, for the latter to provide mapping and test documents with Subscriber’s Partner (PG&E) to ensure that the services are configured to communicate them correctly. Upon completion of successful testing, Xebec shall provide subscribe with usernames, ID(s) and password(s) required to access the ECLynx Web-EDI system for the purpose of sending and receiving data transmissions. The ECLynx Web-EDI system will be connecting to a mailbox setup exclusively for the Subscriber on the nuBridges Added Value Network, for the Prop 39 Energy Operations Facilities Planning & Management Project, in the not-to-exceed amount of $4,000.00, as the selected consultant, with work scheduled to commence on July 1, 2021, through June 30, 2022.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Pays Xebec Data Corporation up to $4,000 to set up energy data exchange with PG&E
summary: Xebec Data Corporation will set up and test an online data-exchange system so the district can send and receive energy-use data with PG&E, the utility, for the Prop 39 energy operations project. The agreement is capped at $4,000 and runs July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
